findings.evidence: "Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Specify what document staff can request a printed copy of (e.g., "a printed copy of the quarterly budget summary").
findings.violation: It is unclear what the "printed copy" refers to - a printed copy of the budget, which was never described as a document, has no stated format, or scope.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Name the specific clock being referenced, e.g., "The 90-day eligibility waiting period resumes on their first day back."
findings.violation: "Stipend clock" has no defined antecedent - it's unclear whether this refers to the 90-day service requirement, the one-claim-per-benefit-year cycle, or something else.

findings.evidence: "A workspace that changes address during the benefit year needs a fresh confirmation before the stipend continues... A workspace confirmation from more than one year ago no longer satisfies the stipend requirement on its own."
findings.fix: Consolidate into a single rule stating when re-confirmation is required (e.g., "annually, or immediately upon any address change").
findings.violation: Two separate triggers for requiring a "fresh confirmation" (address change vs. one-year staleness) are stated without clarifying whether they apply independently, together, or override each other.

findings.evidence: "Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order before the review begins."
findings.fix: Reconcile the two sections into one consistent documentation requirement.
findings.violation: This directly conflicts with Required Documentation, which states "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests" - it's unclear whether an original receipt/PO or a photo is actually required.

findings.evidence: "Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request."
findings.fix: Lay out the application steps as a single ordered list so the submission/review sequence is unambiguous.
findings.violation: This creates a circular process order - documents are said to be submitted "before the review begins" in the first paragraph, yet here the employee reviews a summary before submitting the request, leaving the actual sequence of steps unclear.

findings.evidence: "The manager reviews the request within two business days... The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: State both timeframes in the same units and clarify how the reminder interacts with the review window (e.g., "if the request is still incomplete after three business days").
findings.violation: The relationship between the two-business-day review window and the three-day reminder is unclear, and the units (business days vs. unspecified days) are inconsistent.

findings.evidence: "The manager confirms the equipment category matches the approved list."
findings.fix: Use one consistent term ("equipment catalog") throughout the document.
findings.violation: "Approved list" appears to refer to the "equipment catalog" named in Program Overview, but a different term is used with no indication they are the same thing.

findings.evidence: "Additionally, employees shall retain receipts for one year after the purchase date."
findings.fix: Match the verb style to the rest of the document and resolve whether originals or copies/photos must be retained and for how long.
findings.violation: The sudden switch to "shall retain" breaks from the plain, direct phrasing used everywhere else in the document, and conflicts with How to Apply's requirement to submit the original receipt/PO before any review occurs.

findings.evidence: "The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount."
findings.fix: State the actual stipend amount or reimbursement cap and the criteria finance uses to evaluate receipts.
findings.violation: A section titled "Reimbursement Amounts" never states any actual amount, cap, or percentage - "an evaluation" is vague and gives no criteria for what is approved.

findings.evidence: "this office may ask for a brief photo check once a year"
findings.fix: Name the specific office responsible (e.g., "the benefits team may ask for...").
findings.violation: "This office" has no clear antecedent - the preceding sentence refers to "the applicant," not any office, so it's unclear which team performs the photo check.

findings.evidence: "the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk..."
findings.fix: Split into separate sentences: state the one-device-per-category default rule, then state the second-device exception and its conditions separately.
findings.violation: This is an extremely long run-on sentence that also self-contradicts - it states a "one device per category" rule while simultaneously describing conditions for approving a "second device" in the same breath, without clearly marking the second device as an exception.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Either rename the section to reflect its actual content (a process description) or replace it with actual term definitions, and use consistent third-person phrasing.
findings.violation: The section heading promises definitions of terminology, but the content instead describes a process in second-person voice ("you"), breaking from the third-person voice ("employees," "the applicant") used everywhere else in the document.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Merge this content into How to Apply or remove the redundant section, and list all required steps consistently with that section.
findings.violation: This single-sentence section duplicates content already covered in How to Apply without adding detail, and the comma before "and" is grammatically unnecessary; it also omits the manager approval form and purchase order required elsewhere.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicated text or state consistently which team/role owns the budget review.
findings.violation: This duplicates the Program Overview sentence almost verbatim but attributes budget review to "the finance liaison" instead of "the benefits team," contradicting the earlier statement of ownership.

findings.evidence: "The team then routes the request to the correct approver based on department."
findings.fix: Clarify whether the approver is always the manager or determined by department, and make the two sections consistent.
findings.violation: This conflicts with Approval Timeline, which states "the manager reviews the request," leaving it unclear whether the approver is always the employee's manager or varies "based on department."

findings.evidence: "Once approved, the team schedules the reimbursement for the next pay cycle."
findings.fix: Define a single approval chain (e.g., manager approves eligibility, finance approves amount) and reference it consistently across sections.
findings.violation: This implies the benefits team grants final approval, which conflicts with Reimbursement Amounts ("the finance office... approves the amount") and Approval Timeline ("the manager reviews the request") - three different parties are each described as approving the request.

findings.evidence: "The escalation of repeat requests happens automatically within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Define what constitutes a "repeat request" and reconcile this with the one-claim-per-year eligibility limit.
findings.violation: "Repeat requests" is never defined, and it's unclear how a repeat request could occur given Eligibility's rule that the stipend "covers one claim per employee per benefit year."

findings.evidence: "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Assign budget tracking to a single named team and remove the duplicated, conflicting restatements.
findings.violation: This is the third conflicting attribution of budget tracking responsibility in the document (after "the benefits team" in Program Overview and "the finance liaison" in Special Cases), and it also conflates budget-tracking with the catalog-updating duty assigned to people operations earlier.
